# I-49 slices: silent restore (rung 2) and `PlatformBackupStore`

Staging: `/Users/vlad/Repos/pk-wt/_merge` (`integ/next-stage` @ `86ddd7bfc6`), read only. Plan:
`plan-auto-sign-in.md` §1 rung 2, scenario 8, §2.6 tables, §3 Restore row, §4 privacy and threat
row, SR-3, D-A11; `plan-combined.md` R-6, R-7, R-11, R-15; `I-44-I-45-slices.md` Q-2 and §7–§8;
`I-48-slices.md` §6; `U-sync-clients-slices.md` U-39.5 and U-39.10. Planner: Opus 5.5, 2026-10-28.

**Documents only, no code.** No branch, no code, no corpus, no generated file. The owner approved
every v0.10 plan on 2026-10-28. Each decision below takes the recommended option and records it.
★ marks a wire or plan-mode slice. All ★ slices are approved under CC-01 and this file.

**Wire summary.** No signed document changes. `PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays 5, `DISCOVERY_VERSION` 2
and `corpusVersion` 2. The changes are all additive and unsigned:

- one grant on the existing `token` route;
- one route, `restore` (POST and DELETE);
- one discovery member and one endpoint;
- one table, one launch gate, one product setting and its manifest member;
- one feature id and new transcripts.

There is no new error code and no corpus change. `device-proof.json` already holds a valid
`restore` vector. The line format does not change; only the route defines the value. Plan mode
applies (shared-protocol, V5 text, transcripts).

## 0. Facts on staging (the code wins)

- **The ladders skip rung 2.** Swift `PolarisKeyIdentity/AutoSignIn.swift:4` and Kotlin
  `identity/.../AutoSignIn.kt:4` say "rung 2 silent restore (I-49): skipped here". Godot's I-48.2
  does the same (I-48 is `todo`).
- **The proof.** V5 §12.11.1 already lists purpose `restore`. Its vector is
  `device-proof.json:156` (value nonce-shaped, line 6 `-`), from `tools/corpus/deviceProof.ts:174`.
- **The exchange is the template.** `passthrough/exchange.ts:123-372` runs: shape, rate limit,
  stateless proof, held key, consume, terms, `consentState` → `confirm`, then
  `bindAndAnswer(…, silentSingle: true)`. The gate-off answer is
  `400 unsupported_grant_type` (`passthrough/token.ts:187-194`).
- **Device lifecycle (R-7).** `core/devices/lifecycle.ts` sends the events `bound`, `unbound`,
  `removed` and `keys` through `contributes.onDeviceChange`. Account × product data registers
  through `contributes.subjectStores` (`core/accounts/subjectHooks.ts`; the Connect and Sync
  `index.ts` files show the pattern).
- **Sign-out.** `POST identity/signout` lives in `attach.ts` (V5 §12.3 rule 5). It drops the
  binding, and `unbound` fires.
- **Swift.** `PolarisKeyPlatform/SecureStore.swift` is the data-protection keychain, never
  synchronizable, behind a `KeychainBackend` seam (:35). Godot reaches it through `pkp_call`'s
  `kc_*` ops (`Host.swift:213, :376`).
- **Kotlin.** `:platform` has `main/SecureStore.kt`. The flavour split follows the
  `FlavorIdentity.kt` and `FlavorIntegrity.kt` pattern. `libs.versions.toml` pins credentials
  1.6.0 and googleid 1.2.0, with no Block Store line.
- **Godot export.** `android_export.gd:31` `PLAY_DEPENDENCIES` holds Play Core only. I-48.5b adds
  the Credential Manager pins and a drift test against `libs.versions.toml`.
- **Block Store 16.4.0** (checked 2026-10-28 on Google Maven):
  - released 2024-07-25, 826 days old, and still the latest;
  - minSdk 21, with no AAR metadata constraints;
  - depends on base 18.5.0, basement 18.4.0, tasks 18.2.0 and kotlin-stdlib 1.9.0;
  - already on the classpath through credentials-play-services-auth 1.6.0, so pinning it changes
    no resolution;
  - its API is confirmed in the classes: `StoreBytesData.Builder.setBytes/setKey/setShouldBackupToCloud`,
    `retrieveBytes(RetrieveBytesRequest.setKeys)`, `deleteBytes(DeleteBytesRequest.setKeys)`,
    `isEndToEndEncryptionAvailable()`, `MAX_ENTRY_COUNT` (16) and `MAX_SIZE` (4 KB).
- **Migrations** end at `0148_operator_prefs.sql`. `TABLE_OWNERS.identity` has no restore row.

## 1. Design (recorded decisions)

**D-1 Redeem is a grant on `token`** (rec.; alt. a dedicated redeem route).
`POST /<p>/identity/token`, form-encoded, with `X-PKey-Device`:

| Parameter        | Value                                                                                                             |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `grant_type`     | `urn:polaris-key:grant-type:restore`                                                                              |
| `client_id`      | product slug                                                                                                      |
| `restore_id`     | `rk_` + 22 base64url characters                                                                                   |
| `restore_secret` | `rs_` + 43 base64url characters (32 random bytes)                                                                 |
| `device_key`     | the device's signing key                                                                                          |
| `agree_key`      | the device's agreement key                                                                                        |
| `proof`          | `pkey-proof/1`, purpose `restore`, value `<restore_id>.<device_key>`, line 6 = b64url SHA-256 of `restore_secret` |
| `license_choice` | `app` (default) or `card`                                                                                         |
| `device_name`    | as V5 §12.7.1                                                                                                     |

- **Check order:**
  1. shape and rate limit;
  2. the proof (stateless);
  3. the held signing key must equal `device_key`;
  4. look the row up by id and compare `HMAC(pepper, secret)` in constant time;
  5. consume the row with a compare-and-set delete (`WHERE id=? AND secret_hash=?`, one change);
  6. resolve the subject to an active account through merge aliases;
  7. refuse an `agreeKey` held elsewhere;
  8. terms, then consent (`confirm`);
  9. `bindAndAnswer(silentSingle: true)` and `registerDeviceKeys(…, {via: "restore"})`.
- Every failure is `400 invalid_grant`, with no oracle. A wrong secret does not consume the row.
  A store failure is `503 unavailable`.
- The answers are §12.11.3's table less `interstitial_required` `no_link`: a token with
  `issued_token_type` device, `confirm`, `choose`, `terms`, `not_entitled`, `device_limit`,
  `license_choice_required` or `429`.
- With the gate or setting off, or Identity off, the answer is `400 unsupported_grant_type`.
- Restore never writes `signin-fresh`. Audit `signin.restore` names the target device and never
  the secret.

**D-2 One row per (product, device). The subject's live rows count as "current"** (rec.; alt. one
row per subject, which breaks Android, where each backup carries its own device's key).

**D-3 A row is consumed on first use.** The new device re-enrols, so rotation happens on use
(rec.; alt. reusable until sign-out).

**Enrol and revoke: `POST|DELETE /<p>/identity/restore`** (device bearer, `cors: true`,
`no-store`).

- **POST** takes `{restoreId?}`.
  - `200 {"status":"current"}` when `restoreId` is a live row of this product and subject.
    `checked_at` is bumped.
  - Otherwise `201 {"restoreId","secret"}`, which replaces this device's row. At most 10 rows per
    (product, subject); the oldest by `checked_at` goes.
  - `403 account_required` when the device holds no sign-in binding.
  - `404 not_found` when the feature is off.
  - Also `400 bad_request`, `401` and `429`.
- **DELETE** deletes this device's row and answers `204`, idempotently.

**Revoke paths:**

- `identity/signout` deletes the device's row in the same request, before it answers.
- The identity `onDeviceChange` listener deletes the row on `unbound` and `removed`.
- Removing the app in Connected apps deletes the subject's rows for that product.
- The subject store `identity.restore` deletes on merge (the loser) and on deletion, and exports
  `{createdAt, checkedAt}` per row with no hash.
- Product deletion deletes the product's rows.
- Maintenance purges rows with no check in 180 days (**D-9**).

**D-4 Email on restore** (rec.; alt. none, per D-A13). `appDeviceApprovedNotice` gains `via:
"restore"`: "{app} signed in on {device} from your backup". It goes to the primary address. This
is detection for the Apple ID and Google account residual.

**Rate limits** (`core/rateLimit.ts`, all failing closed):

| Bucket                  | Limit                          |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `identityRestore`       | 10 a minute per client network |
| `identityRestoreDevice` | 5 a minute per device          |
| `identityRestoreKey`    | 10 a day per device            |
| `identityRestoreKeyNet` | 20 a minute per network        |

**D-10 Gates.**

- The launch gate is `launch.identityRestore`, off by default (`core/settings/launchGates.ts`).
- **D-6 Developer opt-out, default on:**
  - the product setting `identity.restore` (row-backed, claimable, on unless switched off; the
    console toggle sits under Identity → App sign-in);
  - the manifest member `identity.restore: boolean`, mutation code `invalid_identity_restore`,
    schema `rejects`;
  - the SDK option `AutoSignInOptions.restore = true`. Set to false, it skips rung 2, never
    enrols, sends `DELETE restore` and deletes this app's restore item.
- Discovery's identity fragment gets `restore: true` and endpoint `restore` only while Identity,
  the setting and the gate all allow it.
- Rows stay inert while the feature is off, and the 180-day sweep removes them.

**Table `identity_restore_keys`.** Owner `identity`. Migration `00XX_identity_restore_keys.sql`;
the lead assigns the number at merge. Rollback is `scripts/rollback/00XX_identity_restore_keys.down.sql`.
Expand-only, with no foreign keys or cascades.

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS identity_restore_keys (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, product TEXT NOT NULL, device_id TEXT NOT NULL, subject TEXT NOT NULL,
  secret_hash TEXT NOT NULL, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, checked_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (product, device_id));
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS identity_restore_keys_subject ON identity_restore_keys (product, subject);
```

**`PlatformBackupStore`.** One per native SDK. It holds only named items:
`restore(product)` and `syncRoot(product, subject, ringId)` for U-39.

- **Swift** (`PolarisKeyPlatform/PlatformBackupStore.swift`):
  - item attributes: `kSecClassGenericPassword`, `kSecAttrSynchronizable: true`,
    `kSecAttrAccessible: kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlock` (a synchronizable item cannot be
    `ThisDeviceOnly`) and `kSecUseDataProtectionKeychain: true`;
  - `kSecAttrAccessGroup` = `accessGroup` when the app passes one (**D-7**: the default is the
    app's default group; pass a `TEAMID.group` to share across a developer's apps);
  - the restore item is service `pkey-restore:<product>`, account `restore`. The sync root is
    service `pkey-sync:<product>`, account `<subject>:<ringId>`;
  - a service outside the two prefixes is refused;
  - the value is at most 4 KB of JSON, `{"v":1,"restoreId","secret"}`;
  - the store reuses the `KeychainBackend` seam;
  - `-34018` (missing entitlement) and `errSecNotAvailable` map to `unavailable`, never a crash.
- **Kotlin:**
  - the port `PlatformBackupStore` lives in `:core` (`get(key)`, `set(key, bytes)`,
    `delete(key)`, `cloudBackup: Boolean`);
  - `:platform` main holds `PlatformBackup.create(context)`. The `play` flavour implements it as
    `BlockStoreBackup` (`setShouldBackupToCloud(isEndToEndEncryptionAvailable())`, **D-5**). The
    `direct` flavour answers unavailable;
  - the `:android` glue adapts it to the port;
  - keys are `pkey-restore-<product>` and `pkey-sync-<product>`. There is one key per product,
    because the app's limit is 16 entries; U-39.10 puts subject and ringId in the value. Whether
    the key charset allows these names is [U] for the builder;
  - the pin is `play-services-auth-blockstore = "16.4.0"` as `playImplementation`.
    `check_flavours.sh` asserts that `direct` has no `com/google/android/gms/auth/blockstore`.
- **Godot** (**D-8**; native lanes only, desktop and web N/A):
  - Apple: the `pkp_call` ops `bk_get`, `bk_set` and `bk_delete` in `Host.swift` over the Swift
    store;
  - Android: the same ops in the plugin's `PlayCommands.kt` over `:platform`, with `DirectCommands`
    answering unavailable;
  - Block Store 16.4.0 goes into `PLAY_DEPENDENCIES`, which I-48.5b's drift test checks;
  - GDScript: `addons/polaris_key/core/store/platform_backup.gd` (`PKeyPlatformBackup`).

**Rung 2 in each ladder** (the same rules everywhere).

- **When it runs.** After rung 1 misses, with no `explicitSignOut`, with discovery `restore`
  present and `options.restore` true, and when the store yields a restore item.
- **The steps.** The device keys come from the existing key store and are generated if missing.
  The client sends the proof, then the grant.
  - On `200`, it stores the token with provenance `signin`, then enrols and writes the new item.
    The result is `signedIn`.
  - On `confirm` or `choose`, it returns the same result as the exchange; enrolment follows
    `complete`.
  - On `invalid_grant`, Android deletes its local item. Apple does not delete: a synchronizable
    delete reaches every device, and a newer write may be on its way. The ladder goes on to
    rung 3.
  - On `429`, `503`, a network failure or an unavailable store, the item is left alone and the
    ladder goes on to rung 3.
- **Enrolment.** After any completed sign-in, from any rung, and on rung 1 at most once every
  24 h, the client sends `POST restore {restoreId of the item}` and writes the item on a `201`.
  The timestamp lives in the local, non-synced store.
- **Sign-out** (scenario 8 and R-11). The client flushes Sync and calls `signout` (the server
  revokes), then deletes the restore item whatever the answer: Apple deletes the synchronizable
  item on every device; the other devices re-enrol at their daily check, and this device's flag
  stops it from using the item. It never touches the sync-root item. Only Reset encryption, Start
  over and account deletion remove that one.
- Nothing logs the secret. The item value and the result redact it.

**Deployed clients and Workers.**

- The Worker ships first, with the gate off. SDKs v0.9.x and earlier ignore `restore` and never
  enrol.
- A new SDK against an old Worker finds no member, skips rung 2 and never enrols.
- On rollback the table goes unread. Items in people's backups stay inert: a redeem answers
  `unsupported_grant_type`, which counts as a failed rung. On roll-forward, rows within 180 days
  still work.

## 2. V5 text and transcripts (★ I-49.3, I-49.8)

**V5 text:**

- new §12.11.8 "Silent restore": the grant, the enrol route, revocation, limits, gates and
  discovery;
- §12.3 rule 5: sign-out deletes the device's restore key;
- §12.11.1: the `restore` value is defined in §12.11.8;
- §12.11.6: the discovery members;
- §13.11.5: the restore item is separate, and sign-out deletes it and keeps the root item;
- §15.8 "Registration": a fourth entry point, restore.

**Transcripts** (`packages/worker/test/transcripts/scenarios/restore.ts`, new):

| Transcript                   | Covers                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `restore-happy`              | enrol, redeem on a second device, re-enrol, the `current` check                                                                                                                                     |
| `restore-confirm`            | consent changed                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `restore-errors`             | wrong secret (no consume), spent row, bad proof, foreign key, `account_required`, `429`, and a valid secret presented to another product (`invalid_grant`, the row not consumed)                    |
| `restore-signout`            | sign-out, then the old secret is refused; and A signs out while B holds a key under the same subject: A's `POST restore` with B's id gets a `201`, and B's old secret is refused after A's sign-out |
| `restore-gate-off`           | `unsupported_grant_type`, enrol `404`                                                                                                                                                               |
| `discovery-identity-restore` | discovery with the members present                                                                                                                                                                  |

**Amendments after the security review** (V5 §12.11.8 is normative; where the text above differs, it wins).

- **Product binding.** Redeem finds the key by id and the product `client_id` names; the consume is
  `WHERE id AND product AND secret_hash`. A secret presented to another product is `invalid_grant`
  and the row is not consumed (conformance case in `restore-errors`).
- **`current` is per device.** `200 current` needs `device_id` equal to the caller and a row under
  90 days old; anything else is `201`. The case in `restore-signout`: A signs out, then B's old
  secret is refused.
- **Revocation does not depend on gates.** Every deletion, `DELETE` (`204` when off) and the
  180-day sweep run whatever the gate, the setting or Identity say; only `POST` and the grant are
  gated, the gate is checked before the lookup, and the operator has a "purge all restore keys"
  action. `complete` does not re-check the gate.
- **`confirm`.** `consent.as` is `{provider: null, email: null}` (`RestoreConsentView`); the notice
  email goes out when the sign-in completes, `via: "restore"` carried on the pending grant.
- **Also adopted.** Removing a device that signed in by restore deletes all the subject's keys for
  the product; the email has a "Remove this device" link (to Polaris Locker's Devices section, no device id) and
  Devices says "Signed in from backup" (DEVICE-REMOVAL); the client queues a failed `DELETE restore` for the next launch; the explicit sign-out
  flag lives outside the backup and only an interactive sign-in clears it; the HMAC is computed
  for a missing row; a key consumed and then refused sends the client to rung 3.

- A Node reference case goes in `conformance/runners/node/restoreTranscripts.test.ts`.
- `features.json` gains `identity.restore`, with proof transcripts and N/A for node, python, web,
  jvm, windows, linux and desktop-bridge. Its parity rows are `planned`: Swift I-49.10, Kotlin
  I-49.12 (except `jvm`), Godot I-49.15 (except linux, windows and web). React, Node and Python
  are N/A.
- `pnpm gen transcripts constants parity docs-reference settings`.

## 4. Threat model and privacy

The THREAT-MODEL rows extend "Platform sign-in" and replace the one-line I-49 row:

| Threat                      | Control                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Residual                                                                 |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Stolen backup secret        | E2E stores only (iCloud Keychain; Block Store cloud only when E2E is available); one use; one product, never the account or the card; refused unless the enrolling device is still signed in and the account has a reachable address; a security notice to every verified address on use; Sign out everywhere ends every key; 5 restores a day per account | Apple ID or Google account compromise, for one sign-in per stored secret |
| Replay of a redeem          | CAS consume; the proof binds the device key and the secret hash                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | The device itself                                                        |
| Restore loop after sign-out | Server row deleted in the sign-out request; item deleted; `explicitSignOut` skips rungs 2–4                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Other devices re-enrol, which this device ignores                        |
| Database leak               | Peppered HMAC only                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | None                                                                     |
| Cross-developer read        | Keychain access group is the developer's team; Block Store is per app and signing key                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Apps of the same team, by design (D-7)                                   |
| Oracle                      | One `invalid_grant` body; wrong secret does not consume                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | None                                                                     |
| Shared Apple ID             | The last writer's account restores; Help says so                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Accepted                                                                 |

**PRIVACY row.** `identity_restore_keys` holds the id, product, device id, pairwise subject, the
peppered HMAC of the secret, and `created_at` and `checked_at`. A row is kept until:

- the device signs out or is removed;
- the app is removed from Connected apps;
- 180 days pass without a check;
- the account or the product is deleted.

The secret lives only on the person's devices and in their iCloud Keychain or Google backup. The
export includes the dates and never the hash.

## 7. Owner steps

- **OS-12** (existing): the Apple keychain access group for the probe and test apps.
- **Real devices:**
  - two Apple devices on one Apple ID: sign in on A, install on B, and B signs in silently;
  - an Android phone: back up, then set up a new phone from that backup;
  - sign out on A, and B no longer restores until it re-enrols.

The lead mirrors these into `~/Downloads/polaris-key-owner-steps.md`.
